note: Round 10 needed both halves of the mechanism, and the reason is a timing fact worth keeping. A cleared_at alone could not close this window honestly: round 10's own last remediation (the Seaside petunia hero, 23:03:53) landed AFTER the two out-of-round write sets below (22:49 and ~22:55-23:05), so any closing edge early enough to allow them would have claimed the round was finished while it demonstrably was not. The round-8 precedent applies verbatim — no window holding a round's real work can exclude a pass that ran first — so the two sets are waived by name and the window is closed as of the moment everything was actually done.

allow.why: The 2026-07-30 WCVP tail (PR #137): 475 plants outside every round manifest validated against Kew's checklist via cross-check-native-region.ts, 53 corrected. The tail is by definition out-of-round — these are rounds 1-5 era rows that predate the manifests — so every correction it makes must land outside round 10's scope, and there is no scope it could land inside instead. Safe as a column waiver rather than 53 named rows because a round-10 plant's own native_region write is IN scope and therefore never becomes a finding here: this entry can only ever match a row round 10 did not seed.

cleared_why: Round 10 is finished: 10/10 pipeline steps, 6/6 artifacts, verify-round --round 10 at 0 failures, and the catalog archive re-captured after the Seaside petunia hero write that had made it stale (PR #139 — the book-end trap, caught by round-progress rather than hours later). Closed now for the reason the round-9 entry gives: the window is baseline-to-now, so leaving it open makes every later catalog-wide pass read as this round's failure, which is how round 8 accumulated 287 false failures. This window had already started doing exactly that to two concurrent sessions. The two write sets that predate this edge are waived by name above rather than swallowed by an early cleared_at, so the record still says who wrote what and why.
